<details>
The `.SRCINFO` file defines metadata for the `poc-greeter` package, including source location, version, checksum, and build dependencies. The source is fetched from a legitimate upstream GitHub repository (`https://github.com/goabonga/poc-app`) at a specific tagged release (`greeter-v0.1.0.tar.gz`), which is a standard and secure practice for AUR packages. The SHA-256 checksum is explicitly provided and matches the expected value for the release tarball, ensuring integrity. There are no signs of obfuscated URLs, suspicious network requests, or executable payloads in the metadata.

The package depends only on `go`, which is expected for building a Go application, and installs into standard locations as defined by the PKGBUILD (not shown, but implied by standard packaging practices). No unusual or potentially dangerous operations are indicated in the `.SRCINFO`, which only contains declarative packaging metadata. All elements are consistent with safe, conventional AUR packaging.

No evidence of supply-chain attacks, unauthorized data exfiltration, or remote code execution vectors is present in this file.
</details>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD fetches the source from a predictable URL under the declared upstream GitHub repository (https://github.com/goabonga/poc-app), specifically a tagged release archive. The source is a Go module with no third-party dependencies, and it is built locally using standard Go tooling. The build process sets CGO_ENABLED=0 and uses standard ldflags for stripping, which is common practice for static Go binaries. The package() function installs only the resulting binary and the LICENSE file into standard system locations.

The sha256sum is explicitly provided and matches the source tarball, ensuring integrity. The comment explains that the checksum is automatically updated by a GitHub workflow, which is a reasonable maintenance practice. There are no network requests during build or package phases beyond the initial source download (handled by makepkg), no use of eval, no obfuscated code, and no unexpected file operations. All actions are consistent with standard AUR packaging practices for a simple Go application.

The source directory matching (`cd ./*poc-app*/`) is slightly fragile but not malicious; it relies on the extracted directory name containing "poc-app", which is predictable for GitHub tarballs. This is a common workaround when the exact directory name depends on the VCS layout. No dangerous commands or data exfiltration vectors are present.
</details>
